title: The Sharp Numerical-Range Spectral-Set Inequality
content: We give a proof of the finite-dimensional scalar form of Crouzeix's conjecture: for every complex matrix A and every rational function r whose poles lie off the numerical range W(A), ||r(A)||_2 <= 2 max_{z in W(A)} |r(z)|. The argument first treats real-analytic strictly convex outer domains. It combines a positive normalized operator-valued double-layer kernel, conjugate Cauchy companions for all powers of finite Blaschke products, Fourier cancellation, and a bounded-sequence recurrence that excludes a singular value larger than 2. Schur approximation and a convex outer approximation then yield the polynomial and rational statements.
